samples.summary: `OfflineRuntime` and its `offerRecoverableWork` loop have no test at all
samples.evidence: Globbed `packages/frontend/**/*offline*` and grepped for `OfflineRuntime` across the package: the only hits are the component itself and `PrivateRoute.tsx`. There is no `offline-runtime.test.tsx`. Untested behavior includes: the once-per-session `collectStale()` sweep, installing `watchForOfflineDisable` with getters, calling `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` on mount and `undefined` on cleanup (which is the *only* thing that makes logout's erase work at all), the `cancelled()` guard after awaits, skipping archives whose `describeArchivedDocument` returns undefined, the `fetchDocument` title fallback to "Untitled", and the whole recover-on-click path (`refused === 'empty'` vs unreadable messaging, the incomplete-copy description, the Open/navigate action). If any of this regresses, the user's unreconcilable work is silently never offered back — the one thing the archive exists for — and nothing in the suite fails.

samples.summary: New `purgeOfflineDocuments` wiring in deleteDocument/deleteDocuments is untested, and the existing suite passes whether or not it is correct
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.test.ts` imports and exercises `deleteDocument` and `deleteDocuments` (lines 112, 136-141) but never mocks or asserts `@/lib/offline-erase`. Because `purgeOfflineDocuments` no-ops when `signedInUserId` is undefined (offline-erase.ts:93), those tests pass identically with the purge call present, absent, or moved outside the `if (response.ok)` guard. The diff's own comment says purging a document the server did *not* delete "would delete unsent work the user can still push" — that exact invariant (purge only on `ok`, and only for `result.deleted`) has no test. `deleteDocuments` test at line 137 returns `{deleted:["a"]}` and asserts only the return value.

samples.summary: `logout()` calling `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` has no test; auth.test.ts has no logout coverage
samples.evidence: Grepped `logout` in `packages/frontend/tests/api/auth.test.ts` — no matches. `offline-erase.test.ts` tests `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` in isolation (lines 250-273) but nothing asserts that `logout()` calls it, that it is awaited before the redirect, or that a throwing erase cannot fail the sign-out. Removing that line leaves the signed-out account's document content on a shared device's disk, silently, with every suite green.

samples.summary: No test covers that the share route actually wraps itself in `NonDurableScope`
samples.evidence: `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` ("never persists anything reached through a share link") wraps `CollabDocumentProvider` in `NonDurableScope` by hand inside the test, so it only proves the context mechanism works — it says nothing about `shared-document.tsx`. Grepping `NonDurableScope` finds it in `use-durable-document.ts`, the durable test, and `shared-document.tsx` only; there is no test that renders `SharedDocumentInner`/the share route and asserts non-durability. Deleting the wrapper from the route would persist other people's shared documents to a visitor's disk with no test failing — which is the case the diff's own comment calls out as revocation-proof leakage.

samples.summary: The Settings offline toggle (render + `onCheckedChange` wiring) has no test
samples.evidence: Grepped `settings` case-insensitively under `packages/frontend/tests` — the four hits are date-format, theme-provider, notification-text and date-cell; there is no settings page test. `offline-persistence-preference.test.ts` covers the setter/subscriber module, but nothing asserts the Switch is rendered, reflects `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled()`, or is wired to `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled`. A broken toggle means the user cannot turn the feature off (and therefore cannot trigger the promised erase).

samples.summary: `reportLoss` flipping published durability to false is never tested through the provider
samples.evidence: In `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` ("latches on the SDK's dropped-changes event") the only assertion is `expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith('note-7')` on `store.expectLoss`. Nothing asserts that `durable.reportLoss()` was called or that the context value subsequently reads `durable: false`. `use-sync-status.test.ts` supplies `durable: false` directly via a hand-made `DurableDocumentScope` value, so the link from the SDK event to the chip's promise is untested end-to-end: a provider that latched `expectLoss` but never set `lost` would keep claiming "Saved to this device" after the SDK dropped the work — the one direction the code says it must never fail in.

samples.summary: Snapshot-vs-append race assertion is satisfiable by an implementation that discards concurrent appends entirely
samples.evidence: The assertion is `expect(seqs.length === 0 || seqs.join() === "2").toBe(true)` plus `expect(seqs).not.toContain(1)`. Both hold for a store that silently drops every append racing a `saveSnapshot` — i.e. loses the user's edit — so the case cannot distinguish "compaction won" from "the append was thrown away". The neighbouring concurrent-loads case guards this with a final `changeCount` check; this one has no such anchor.

samples.summary: The new `saved-locally` tooltip wording is not asserted anywhere
samples.evidence: `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` asserts the label `Saved to this device` and the absence of destructive styling, but greps for the tooltip text ("will be sent when syncing") return nothing; only the pre-existing `not-saved` tooltip has a comment about wording at line 391. The new branch of `tooltipFor` is uncovered.

samples.summary: Comment claims coverage by a test file that does not exist
samples.evidence: The added comment says "`durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` covers the nesting", but globbing `packages/frontend/**/*durable*` returns no such file — the nesting is covered by `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx`. A dangling pointer to non-existent coverage is exactly the kind of note that lets a future reader assume a gap is filled.

finding.summary: `OfflineRuntime` and its `offerRecoverableWork` loop have no test at all
finding.evidence: Globbed `packages/frontend/**/*offline*` and grepped for `OfflineRuntime` across the package: the only hits are the component itself and `PrivateRoute.tsx`. There is no `offline-runtime.test.tsx`. Untested behavior includes: the once-per-session `collectStale()` sweep, installing `watchForOfflineDisable` with getters, calling `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` on mount and `undefined` on cleanup (which is the *only* thing that makes logout's erase work at all), the `cancelled()` guard after awaits, skipping archives whose `describeArchivedDocument` returns undefined, the `fetchDocument` title fallback to "Untitled", and the whole recover-on-click path (`refused === 'empty'` vs unreadable messaging, the incomplete-copy description, the Open/navigate action). If any of this regresses, the user's unreconcilable work is silently never offered back — the one thing the archive exists for — and nothing in the suite fails.

verdict.reason: No test anywhere in the repository exercises `OfflineRuntime` or `offerRecoverableWork`. Repo-wide greps for `OfflineRuntime|offerRecoverableWork|offline-runtime` return exactly three files (the component, `PrivateRoute.tsx`, and a task doc) and a repo-wide glob `**/*offline-runtime*` returns only the component itself. The sole production mount is `PrivateRoute.tsx:35`; grepping `PrivateRoute` repo-wide shows no test renders it (the only test hit, navigation-guard.test.tsx:168, is a comment). Behavior-string searches ("Save a copy", "could not be reconciled", "offline-recovery-") hit no test file. Library-level suites exist (offline-erase.test.ts, offline-copy.test.ts, offline-copy-recovery.test.ts, wafflebase-doc-store-*.test.ts) and the nearest component-level hit is collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:290 calling `store.collectStale(0)` directly on the store — that covers the store, not the runtime's once-per-session sweep, the `cancelled()` guard after awaits, the getter-based `watchForOfflineDisable` install, the `rememberOfflineUser(userId)`/`rememberOfflineUser(undefined)` mount-cleanup pair (the only thing that makes logout's erase work), the `describeArchivedDocument` skip, the 'Untitled' title fallback, or the recover-on-click messaging/navigate path. Blocking under the test-adequacy rubric: this component runs for every signed-in user and is the sole caller of the logout-erase priming and the recovery offer, so a regression silently loses the user's unreconcilable work or leaves local data unerased on a shared device, with nothing in the suite failing.

finding.summary: New `purgeOfflineDocuments` wiring in deleteDocument/deleteDocuments is untested, and the existing suite passes whether or not it is correct
finding.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.test.ts` imports and exercises `deleteDocument` and `deleteDocuments` (lines 112, 136-141) but never mocks or asserts `@/lib/offline-erase`. Because `purgeOfflineDocuments` no-ops when `signedInUserId` is undefined (offline-erase.ts:93), those tests pass identically with the purge call present, absent, or moved outside the `if (response.ok)` guard. The diff's own comment says purging a document the server did *not* delete "would delete unsent work the user can still push" — that exact invariant (purge only on `ok`, and only for `result.deleted`) has no test. `deleteDocuments` test at line 137 returns `{deleted:["a"]}` and asserts only the return value.

verdict.reason: The wiring of purgeOfflineDocuments into deleteDocument/deleteDocuments has no test that can fail. documents.test.ts mocks only ./auth and sonner (lines 3-4); deleteDocument is invoked at line 112 solely to assert URL encoding, and the deleteDocuments test (136-144) asserts only the returned body, URL, method and request body. purgeOfflineDocuments no-ops without a remembered user (offline-erase.ts:95-98) and documents.test.ts never calls rememberOfflineUser, so the suite passes identically whether the purge call is present, removed, hoisted outside the `if (response.ok)` guard, or given `ids` instead of `result.deleted`. offline-erase.test.ts:277-314 tests purgeOfflineDocuments in isolation only — it never goes through the documents API. Wide searches for a counterexample (repo-wide grep for purgeOfflineDocuments, offline-erase, deleteDocument; packages/frontend/tests/**; any test combining WafflebaseDocStore/rememberOfflineUser with the documents API; no e2e directory exists) found none. Impact is major: an incorrect guard would drop local copies of documents the server did not delete, losing unsent offline work.

finding.summary: `logout()` calling `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` has no test; auth.test.ts has no logout coverage
finding.evidence: Grepped `logout` in `packages/frontend/tests/api/auth.test.ts` — no matches. `offline-erase.test.ts` tests `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` in isolation (lines 250-273) but nothing asserts that `logout()` calls it, that it is awaited before the redirect, or that a throwing erase cannot fail the sign-out. Removing that line leaves the signed-out account's document content on a shared device's disk, silently, with every suite green.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `logout()` awaits `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` at packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:105, but no test anywhere in the repo exercises that wiring. I read tests/api/auth.test.ts in full (68 lines): it only covers the fetchWithAuth 401 redirect latch, and although fetchWithAuth calls logout() internally (auth.ts:229) the tests assert only href assignments, so deleting line 105 leaves them green. A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `logout|eraseOffline` (53 files) surfaced no other test touching the caller: offline-erase.test.ts:241-274 tests eraseOfflineDataOnLogout() in isolation against the default store; the wafflebase-doc-store-*.test.ts and use-durable-document.test.tsx hits are comments or store-level dropAllForUser coverage; url.test.ts/image-insert.test.ts hits are the literal string "/auth/logout". No test file imports `logout` from @/api/auth (only fetchWithAuth, fetchMe, fetchMeOptional, fetchYorkieToken, isAuthExpiredError appear), and no test imports or mocks @/lib/offline-erase to observe the call. There is no e2e suite (**/e2e/** empty) and nav-user.tsx, the sign-out UI caller, has no test file. Nothing asserts the erase happens on logout, that it is awaited before redirectTo("/") (auth.ts:116), or that a rejecting erase cannot fail sign-out. Major: silent loss of the guard leaves a signed-out account's document content on a shared device's disk with every suite passing.

finding.summary: No test covers that the share route actually wraps itself in `NonDurableScope`
finding.evidence: `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` ("never persists anything reached through a share link") wraps `CollabDocumentProvider` in `NonDurableScope` by hand inside the test, so it only proves the context mechanism works — it says nothing about `shared-document.tsx`. Grepping `NonDurableScope` finds it in `use-durable-document.ts`, the durable test, and `shared-document.tsx` only; there is no test that renders `SharedDocumentInner`/the share route and asserts non-durability. Deleting the wrapper from the route would persist other people's shared documents to a visitor's disk with no test failing — which is the case the diff's own comment calls out as revocation-proof leakage.

verdict.reason: No test anywhere in the repo exercises the share route's own `NonDurableScope` wrapping. The only test that mentions the scope (collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:176-197) constructs the wrapper by hand around `CollabDocumentProvider`, so it verifies the context mechanism, not `shared-document.tsx`. No test imports/renders `SharedDocumentInner` or `SharedDocumentByToken` for real — the one test that references the module (`template-review-queue.test.tsx:30`) mocks it out, and `shared-blob-routing.test.ts` only imports the pure `sharedBlobKind` helper. `use-durable-document.test.tsx` covers hook policy (including the anonymous-user arm) but not the signed-in share-link visitor the wrapper exists for. No e2e/Playwright spec or source-scanning guard test (the repo does have that pattern in preview-surface.test.tsx / loader.test.tsx) covers it either. Removing `<NonDurableScope>` at shared-document.tsx:982/1058 would keep the suite green while persisting other people's shared documents to a visitor's disk beyond link revocation — a silent, data/privacy-affecting regression, hence major.

finding.summary: The real Web Locks adapter (`webLocks()`) is never exercised; every election test injects a fake lock manager
finding.evidence: In `durable-session.test.ts` every call to `acquireDurableSession` is preceded by `setDurableLockForTest(fakeLocks())` (or by a `navigator.locks`-absent case where `supportsDurableSession()` is false and no request is made). `supportsDurableSession()` short-circuits to `true` whenever `injected` is set, so the `webLocks()` branch in `acquireDurableSession` is unreachable from the suite. That leaves the production code path untested: the `ifAvailable: true` callback contract, `resolve(undefined)` when `lock` is null, and — most importantly — the parked `new Promise<void>(resolveHeld => …)` that is what actually holds and later frees the lock. The `beforeAll` stub installed in the suite (`request: () => Promise.resolve(undefined)`) ignores the callback entirely, so it could not even be used to drive this path (a call would hang). If `webLocks()` is wrong, no tab ever becomes durable (feature dead) or the name is never released (every later tab refused), and the entire green suite of election tests would still pass.

verdict.reason: The real Web Locks adapter is genuinely unexercised. `webLocks()` (durable-session.ts:85-108) is reachable only from acquireDurableSession's `(injected ?? webLocks())` at line 151, which requires `injected === undefined` while `supportsDurableSession()` is true — but supportsDurableSession() returns true unconditionally when `injected` is set (lines 57-60). Every acquire call site across all three test files that use the seam installs a promise-returning fake (durable-session.test.ts:94,111,126,138,150,163,178; use-durable-document.test.tsx:48,61,78,92,...; collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:106-107 beforeEach), and the only non-injected cases (durable-session.test.ts:186-223) delete navigator.locks so no request is issued. A repo-wide multiline grep for `navigator.locks` / `.locks!` shows the callback-style `request(name, {ifAvailable}, cb)` API is invoked nowhere except the production file; the suite's only navigator.locks stub (durable-session.test.ts:15-25) uses `request: () => Promise.resolve(undefined)`, which ignores the callback entirely and could not drive the path. There is no browser-mode or e2e project that could cover it: vite.config.ts:392-402 defines a single jsdom test project over tests/** and src/**, and tests/setup.ts installs no Web Locks polyfill. Impact is major under this lens: the untested code is the parked-promise hold/release contract, so a defect there means either no tab ever becomes durable or the lock name is never released (every later tab refused), while the entire election suite stays green.
